title: Squared pressure mismatch gave no clear six-month RONI uncertainty gain at 1981-2024 origins
abstract: We tested whether squared Southern Oscillation Index mismatch improves six-month relative Nino 3.4 forecast uncertainty. The mismatch is the pressure residual after a temperature-history fit. Both variance models used the same seasonal mean forecast. Earlier-target fits gave 176 test forecasts at 1981-2024 origins. Added mismatch changed mean Gaussian log score by -0.01291 nats, where positive means better. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was -0.05705 to +0.02065. Central 90% interval coverage fell from 85.23% to 83.52%. Primary three- and ten-year block limits also included zero. Recent-period and selected-target checks reversed the point-score sign, with uncertain five-year gains. This test gives no clear added uncertainty skill. It does not establish the absence of physical coupling. Revised and rounded indices, Gaussian models, internal variance fitting, 44 test years and conditional uncertainty limit inference. We provide code, exact external source paths and hashes, aggregate evidence, a figure and numerical audits.

display.caption: Squared pressure mismatch gave no clear primary log-score gain. Bars give conditional 95% five-year block limits. Positive values favor the added variance term.
